gaps.sentence: She kept every receipt ___ she could claim the expenses back.
gaps.explanation: 'So that + could' expresses purpose; 'in case' expresses precaution.

gaps.sentence: My sister is terribly reserved, ___ I'll talk to complete strangers.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two parallel facts: her nature versus mine.

gaps.sentence: She earns a very good salary; ___, she never seems to have any money.
gaps.explanation: 'Yet' contrasts two facts, like but, in a slightly more formal way.

gaps.sentence: ___ the theory is elegant, the data simply don't support it.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' grants the fact (the theory is elegant) before contradicting it.

gaps.sentence: The flight was delayed ___ thick fog.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of' + noun phrase gives the cause; although/despite express contrast.

gaps.sentence: ___ she was utterly exhausted, she stayed to help clear up.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a known fact: she was exhausted and still stayed.

gaps.sentence: ___ you finish early, come and give us a hand.
gaps.explanation: 'If' introduces a real condition; 'in case' would change the meaning to precaution.

gaps.sentence: He neither apologised ___ offered an explanation.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither' pairs with 'nor' in this correlative structure.
